query: Consider the following context: The ability to endure extreme corrosion in challenging environments is reduced in stainless steel. This can be addressed by appropriate surface modification techniques to redefine the surface with the required properties. In that context, which method can be used for improved corrosion resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Nitriding surface modification can improve the corrosion resistance of stainless steel in extreme environments.
generation.material_initial_state: Austenitic stainless steel (e.g., AISI 304) in its annealed state
generation.intervention: Nitriding at 400°C for 2 hours with a nitrogen gas flow rate of 0.1 L/min
generation.conditions: Exposure to a 3.5% NaCl solution at 25°C
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a chromium nitride layer on the surface
generation.mechanism: The chromium nitride layer acts as a barrier to chloride ion penetration, reducing the initiation of pitting corrosion
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% reduction in corrosion rate (mm/year) compared to untreated stainless steel
generation.baseline: Untreated AISI 304 stainless steel exposed to the same conditions
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in corrosion resistance may vary depending on the specific nitriding conditions and the composition of the stainless steel alloy

falsification_experiment.design: Immersion corrosion test in a 3.5% NaCl solution at 25°C for 30 days
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the corrosion rate of the nitrided stainless steel is not at least 20% lower than that of the untreated stainless steel, the hypothesis is falsified
